frontier.note: BESKT PR 6 -- THE GOVERNED CONDUCT PROMPTS AND THE IMMUTABLE REPORT CHAIN. Schema only; no application code on this branch names any object below, so nothing is released against a pending migration. Closes the two gaps the conduct layer left open after PR 5A (20261113090000) and PR 5B: an interviewer could see the frozen themes and questions of a session but had NO governed way to read the permitted follow-up prompts, and a completed interview had no ending -- bcp_conduct_* held positions, entries, verifications, panels and resolutions, and not one of the thirteen PR 5A client RPCs could finalise anything a human could read back. (1) READ SURFACE: bcp_conduct_topic_prompts(uuid) is the only new read path and returns nothing on its own authority -- auth.uid() first, session existence second, then the EXISTING case authority scp_iv_can_read_case(), so a prompt is visible exactly to whoever may already read the case. It never reads the current published method: it resolves the session's FROZEN method_version_id, and answers {available:false, reason} for version_not_found, mode_not_permitted and version_not_published, so a draft, suspended, retired or security-vetting version yields no prompt text at all. Prompts are joined on the frozen exposure_profile_id and the session's own themes and items, and every row must carry permitted_mode='recruitment_support' on BOTH the prompt and its item, with access_class <> 'authorised_security_function'. No client role gains table access to beskt_prompts, which still carries exactly one policy. (2) THE REPORT CHAIN reuses PR #216's architecture (20261107090000) rather than inventing a second one: preview -> blockers -> basis hash -> immutable finalisation -> readback. bcp_conduct_reports is append-only -- RLS ENABLE and FORCE, zero write policies, zero INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants to anon, authenticated or service_role, and a row trigger that refuses every DELETE and permits exactly one UPDATE, final -> superseded, comparing every other column field by field so a supersede cannot smuggle an edit. A partial unique index keeps at most one final report per session. bcp_conduct_basis_hash() deliberately strips {audit_events} before hashing: finalising APPENDS the event the payload carries, so a basis over the whole payload would invalidate itself the instant the report was written and the unchanged-basis branch could never match. The content hash still covers the whole document. The builder bcp_conduct_build_report_basis() is INTERNAL -- granted to service_role only, never to authenticated -- so the assembled basis is reachable only through preview and finalisation, both of which check case authority. (3) NO JUDGEMENT: the migration adds no column named for a score, points, weight, threshold, total, rank, suitability, credibility, truthfulness, recommendation, risk, verdict, deception, hire, confidence, rating, grade or level -- asserted by the postflight against the catalogue, not promised in a comment -- and every payload the chain returns carries produces_score:false, produces_ranking:false, produces_recommendation:false and interpretation:'none'. The report records what was asked, what was said, what was corrected, what was verified, what each assessor independently held, what the panel resolved and what remains unknown. It reaches no conclusion about a person. (4) SEEDS NOTHING: the migration inserts zero reports and zero method content. BESKT v1 is produced through the governance RPCs by real authorised people, never by a migration.

frontier.note: BESKT PR 7 -- THE GOVERNED WAY TO AUTHOR METHOD CONTENT. Schema only; no application code on this branch names any object below. CLOSES A GAP NOBODY HAD NAMED: 20261108090000 built the whole governed LIFECYCLE of a BESKT method -- create, version, submit, review, publish, suspend, retire, grant, revoke, ten RPCs reachable from a browser -- and built no way to author the CONTENT those RPCs move through. beskt_exposure_profiles, beskt_sections, beskt_items, beskt_item_options, beskt_prompts, beskt_routing_rules, beskt_evidence_anchors, beskt_observation_fields and beskt_activation_requirements grant authenticated SELECT and nothing else; ALL goes to service_role; no function in any migration inserts a row into any of them; beskt_touch_draft only recomputes the hash. The database suite's own fixture builds method content by dropping OUT of the authenticated role and writing as the table owner, which is the admission that no client path exists. So a theme, question, option, purpose, prompt, routing rule or exposure profile could only be created as service_role (which must never reach a browser) or inside a migration (which is exactly how production content must NOT be seeded). ADDS NINE DOORS: beskt_author_exposure_profile, _section, _item (options travel with it and are reconciled by key), _prompt, _routing_rule, _evidence_anchor, _observation_field, _activation_requirement, and beskt_delete_content. They are DOORS, NOT LAW: every content invariant already lives in beskt_guard_child_row(), which fires on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for all nine tables and holds against the table owner -- and therefore against these functions, which run as the owner. Draft-only editing, no re-parenting, same-version references, the exposure-profile boundary, the PEACE stage binding, the Evaluation template, routing direction and mode escalation are not restated, because restating them would create a second place to be wrong. What is added in front of that law: auth.uid(); the SAME scp_interview_can_edit() editor role beskt_touch_draft already demands (no new role, no new grant table); replay answered through the existing beskt_operation_begin BEFORE any write; the version locked at the revision the caller saw through the existing beskt_lock_version; draft-or-in-review only, refused by name; the content hash recomputed and the revision advanced exactly as beskt_touch_draft does; an event appended to the existing ledger. PAYLOADS ARE jsonb AND THAT IS A TYPED CONTRACT, NOT A BLOB: an item carries twenty governed columns, so each door takes one object and then REFUSES ANY KEY IT DOES NOT KNOW (beskt_content_reject_unknown_keys) -- a misspelled purpose_sv is refused by name rather than dropped on the floor, and nothing is stored as jsonb; every value lands in the typed column it always had. NO NEW CLIENT DML: not one grant on any content table changes, asserted by the postflight against information_schema. NO JUDGEMENT: no door accepts a score, weight, threshold, rank or verdict because no such column exists, also asserted against the catalogue. SEEDS NOTHING: BESKT v1 is authored by real editors through these doors, never by the migration that opens them.

frontier.note: BESKT PR 5A -- THE GOVERNED CONDUCT OF THE BESKT INTERVIEW. Schema and governed runtime contract only; no application code depends on it while it is pending. Builds on the BESKT governed content (20261108090000), the candidate preparation (20261110090000) and the interview-case bridge (20261112090000), and reuses the EXISTING Interview Intelligence spine rather than duplicating it: the case is scp_interview_cases, the case authority is scp_iv_can_read_case / scp_iv_can_write_case, and the ledger is PR 3's bcp_events written through bcp_record_event. It creates no case, candidate, application or report system of its own. Adds six tables carrying the method's information model as STRUCTURED COLUMNS -- observable fact, candidate explanation, interviewer interpretation, alternative explanation, protective factor, verification need, verification state and source, sensitivity class, correction and its reason, and who recorded each thing and when -- with no score, ranking, verdict or free-form jsonb anywhere. Assessors work independently: a position is invisible to the others until the reader's own is locked, disagreement is recorded rather than averaged, and nothing is reopened once the panel has read it. It also rebuilds the bcp_events CHECK vocabulary to add ten conduct events, which is why the rollback restores PR 4's vocabulary verbatim and refuses to run while any conduct session or conduct event exists. NOT applied to the hosted database: no hosted migration, production write or Lovable publication was performed for this change.

frontier.note: SCHEMA HALF of the Security Passport first-run journey. Adds ONE private table (public.sp_passport_operations), THREE SECURITY DEFINER functions, ONE partial unique index on sp_passport_events, and ONE column on sp_passport_profiles (onboarding_draft_revision). It also TIGHTENS one existing policy -- sp_events_self_insert now refuses a client-written event whose detail carries operation_id or first_merit. No row is rewritten or back-filled and no other existing object changes. THE DEFECT: finishing the first-run wizard performed four independent writes from the browser -- insert the employment period, update the profile, insert two events -- with nothing holding them together, so a failure at any seam left a merit with onboarding still in progress (and the next attempt SKIPPED the insert because a period now existed, leaving the holder unable ever to finish), or a completed profile whose audit events were lost silently because the insert's error was never read. Completion was also not idempotent, and the truthfulness declaration was never checked at all: declared_accurate_at was written unconditionally whenever completion was called, while the tick-box lived only in React state. THE SECOND DEFECT, found by independent review of the first draft of this migration: idempotency was keyed on sp_passport_events.detail->>'operation_id', and that table is directly insertable by authenticated with RLS checking only the holder and actor -- so a signed-in holder could pre-seed an experience_created event carrying any operation id and the function would answer a replay without proving the subject existed, belonged to them, matched the submitted facts, or that onboarding and the declaration had happened. Idempotency now rests on sp_passport_operations, which has NO grant of any kind for anon or authenticated (TRUNCATE included, which RLS does not cover) and RLS enabled and FORCED with no policies, so the Data API cannot reach it; the operation is bound to auth.uid() and to a sha256 fingerprint of exactly the facts submitted, a replay carrying different facts is refused (SP_OPERATION_FACTS_CHANGED), one holder replaying another's id is refused (SP_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT), and a replay is answered only after re-checking that the recorded subject still exists and still belongs to the caller (SP_OPERATION_SUBJECT_MISSING). sp_passport_ensure commits the profile, its receipt and its creation event in one transaction and repairs a legacy profile that has no receipt. The function is NOT a general merit API: a NEW first-merit operation is refused once the holder holds a current merit (SP_FIRST_MERIT_ALREADY_EXISTS), while the original operation still replays -- and that decision is SERIALISED PER HOLDER with a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed to auth.uid(), taken before the receipt is claimed, because two DIFFERENT operation ids do not conflict on the receipt's primary key and would otherwise each see no committed merit and each create one. The lock is released at commit or rollback, so it is not a permanent constraint: a holder whose only merit is later archived returns to the first run. Proved with two psql processes carrying different ids (the second waited 3s and was refused; one merit, one receipt, one event set), and a permanent negative control in db-test.sh strips the lock out of the live definition, watches two merits appear, and re-applies this migration. The declaration is stamped with the time it was MADE rather than coalesced onto a legacy timestamp, and a replay preserves it. It names no trust column at all, so the merit takes the self_declared / active column defaults; the migration's postflight and the database suite both assert that, along with the grants, the RLS state and the absence of any policy on the receipts table. DEPLOY ORDER: SCHEMA FIRST and safe alone -- nothing existing calls the functions, the receipts table starts empty, the index is partial on a key no existing row carries, and the column is additive with a default. The tightened events policy breaks no existing client: every application event insert writes a detail object carrying neither key. The dependent application release is held out of merge by schema-first-release-check.ts until this is recorded applied here. Rolling back drops the three functions, the table, the index and the column, and restores the previous events policy; it touches no holder merit, event or profile row, and the db-test.sh rollback proof asserts exactly that before re-applying over the same data. PHASE 1 OF 3, AND IT IS ADDITIVE. It revokes nothing and breaks nothing, so it can be applied to the live site on its own, with the published application still running unchanged. There is no window to hold open and no 'apply the next thing immediately behind it'.

THE DEFECT. 20261010090000 granted `authenticated` INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on cv_documents with RLS that checked ownership only. A signed-in holder can therefore POST an invented employment history straight to the Data API, and sp_submit_application_with_cv_source would copy it onto an employer-readable job application.

WHAT THIS MIGRATION DOES. It installs the controlled write path BESIDE the open door rather than instead of it: a server-owned idempotency ledger with no client grants, and cv_create / cv_save / cv_refresh_from_profile / cv_delete -- SECURITY DEFINER, owner from auth.uid(), every factual value derived from the caller's own active sp_experience_periods, sp_claims, sp_passport_profiles, security_career_profiles and profiles rows. Requested fact ids are INTERSECTED with what the caller has, so an unknown or stale id can never add information. Presentation is rebuilt key by key against the bundle, so a citation of a fact the person does not have is dropped. Contact details are validated only where switched on. Every mutation requires the revision the caller was looking at and refuses a stale one with CV_CHANGED; CV_NOT_FOUND is the identical answer for absent and not-yours.

Section 1 RESTATES the existing grants rather than revoking them, so nothing the published application does today stops working the moment this is applied. TRUNCATE was never granted and still is not. Assertions P1-P3 of the test suite pin exactly that.

WHY THE OPEN DOOR IS SAFE MEANWHILE. Because the employer boundary is closed in this same migration. sp_submit_application_with_cv_source now re-checks every carried fact BY VALUE against the holder's live records and refuses with CV_DOCUMENT_STALE_FACTS, so a fabricated CV can still be written but can no longer be sent. It also builds the employer's copy through cv_application_snapshot v2: a contact value whose switch is off has its KEY removed, internal sp_* uuids are replaced by snapshot-local keys, the frozen per-credential verified boolean is dropped, and checked_at is added. Expiry is deliberately not a refusal. Group N of the test suite proves both halves -- that a fabricated employment still lands through the open door, and that the boundary refuses to send it.

Functions are named cv_* and not sp_*: they read cd_report_snapshots for the opt-in Career Discovery insight, and security_passport_phase2_test 5.2 forbids an sp_* body from reading a cd_* object.

Phase 1 was applied to production on 2026-09-08, on its own, with the published application still writing cv_documents directly and unaffected -- which is what 'additive' was supposed to mean and is now a fact rather than a plan. Then, and only then, phase 3 -- 20261103090000_cv_documents_lockdown.sql, PR #202 -- which is the migration that actually revokes the direct grants. It refuses to run unless the four cv_* functions are present, and it must stay a draft until the new application is live.
